purpose: Shared guide for interview question shape, voice, and deterministic bad-question detection.
principles: Questions should create information gain, not ask the candidate to self-rate.
Pressure is useful only after frame and clarify establish context.
Use plain spoken English suitable for Indian candidates.
Guide the answer space lightly, then leave an escape hatch such as 'or was there something else?'.
Prefer evidence questions over confidence questions.
Do not ask low-level recall late in the interview unless that surface is explicitly being tested.

frame.goal: Open a claim gently and establish the decision frame.
good_structures: When you changed X, were you mainly trying to improve A, reduce B, test C, or was there something else? Talk me through how you framed that decision.
When you redesigned X, were you mainly reducing latency, memory use, failure rate, or was another constraint more important? Talk me through how you framed it.
bad_structures: Was it A, B, or C?

clarify.goal: Pin down definition, denominator, ownership, scope, or system boundary.
good_structures: What counted in the denominator for that metric, and what was excluded?
Which part did you personally own, and which part came from another team or vendor?
bad_structures: What was the exact SQL script name?

explore.goal: Understand reasoning, behavior change, or mechanism.
good_structures: What user behavior changed after this went live?
Which split would you check first if two interventions launched together?

pressure.goal: Ask one sharp challenge after enough context exists.
good_structures: If conversion improved but refunds also increased, what result would make you rethink the change?
If support calls and KYC UX shipped together, which split would you check first?
bad_structures: How did taxonomy isolate causal impact and what properties did you use and how did you validate it?
What would prove you are not exaggerating?

synthesize.goal: Turn evidence into a fair conclusion and limit overclaim.
good_structures: What should we carry forward as a fair conclusion from this result, and what should we avoid claiming too strongly?
If leadership said the checklist caused the whole lift, what part would you accept and what would you push back on?
bad_structures: Which part are you most confident in?
Which component are you most confident with?

recover.goal: Recover signal from vague, shallow, or honest-gap answers.
good_structures: Which part did you personally handle, even if the rest came from the team?
What is the one part you can still explain clearly?
bad_structures: So you did not really do it?

self_rating.description: Asks the candidate to rate confidence instead of showing evidence.
examples: Which part are you most confident in?
Which component are you most confident with?
What is your strongest area here?

low_signal_implementation_recall.description: Tests tiny implementation memory instead of reasoning or role-relevant depth.
examples: What specific SQL script did you reuse?
Which event property did you add later?

generic_framework.description: Asks abstract framework language after concrete evidence is needed.
examples: What is your framework for attributing lift?
How do you generally approach dashboards?

compound_overload.description: Hides multiple questions in one spoken sentence.
examples: How did taxonomy isolate causal impact and what event properties did you use and how did you validate attribution?

unsupported_internals.description: Assumes internal model/system ownership not supported by resume or answer.
examples: How did you modify the model weights?
What latent representation did your UI control?

product_analytics: What denominator was used for the 42% conversion metric?
If support calls and KYC UX shipped together, which split would you check first?
If leadership said the checklist caused the whole lift, what part would be incomplete about that interpretation?
dashboard_ops: Which dashboard metric caused the most disagreement, and why?
If you removed every dashboard tile except one, which one would stay?
Which metric looked healthy while the business was actually getting worse?
technical_systems: What part did you personally own, and where did the vendor or platform team take over?
What breaks first if traffic doubles during a vendor outage?
Which retry or fallback decision changed the user experience most?
